package_info.package_name: fixedwidthtable (example, applies to all listed packages)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages contain obfuscated or unobfuscated code that, upon installation, exfiltrates sensitive files such as SSH private keys and Kubernetes configuration files to a remote attacker-controlled domain (app.threatest.com). The packages masquerade as legitimate libraries but are designed to steal credentials and system information, violating user trust and npm ecosystem norms.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, collects system information (username, hostname, IP), and exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating private SSH keys and Kubernetes configs during package installation is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it directly compromises user credentials and infrastructure.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages do not access or transmit sensitive user files or system information during installation. This behavior is a clear violation of user trust and package ecosystem norms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate enterprise deployment tool might collect system info for inventory, but would never exfiltrate private keys or configs to an untrusted third-party domain.
key_indicators: Network exfiltration to hardcoded external domain

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, obfuscated code reads sensitive files and system info, then exfiltrates the data to app.threatest.com via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscation is used to hide malicious intent, making it harder for users and automated tools to detect credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely obfuscate installation scripts, especially when accessing sensitive files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for protecting intellectual property, but not for scripts that access user credentials.
key_indicators: References to sensitive file paths and network requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During postinstall, the code collects SSH keys, Kubernetes configs, and system info, then exfiltrates them to app.threatest.com.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly exfiltrating sensitive credentials and configs is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should transmit private keys or configs to an external server during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is always malicious in this context.
key_indicators: Presence of Mandarin comments (possible link to threat actor)

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious npm package (e.g., fixedwidthtable or @am-fe/hooks).
Postinstall script executes, reading sensitive files (SSH keys, Kubernetes configs) and gathering system info.
Collected data is exfiltrated via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: npm package postinstall scripts accessing ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
Network requests to external domains during installation
file_indicators: scripts/index.js with file access and network code
References to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config in package scripts
Presence of Mandarin comments in code
network_indicators: Connections to Cloudflare IPs 172.67.141.49, 104.21.9.30 during install
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that access sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config and make outbound network requests, especially to known malicious domains like app.threatest.com. Flag packages with obfuscated installation scripts or unexplained file access. Use static analysis to detect references to sensitive file paths and dynamic analysis to observe network behavior during installation.
